research_mode: official ONS domestic-abuse overview and criminal-justice statistics only; source-unit, cohort, survey-break and outcome-comparability gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Cross-system case-linkage boundary
verified_claims: Specific domestic-abuse cases cannot be followed directly through every stage of the criminal justice system using the published aggregate datasets.
limitations: Counts at different stages must not be interpreted as one linked case cohort.

sources.name: Different statistical units
verified_claims: Domestic-abuse data can refer to victims, offences, suspects, defendants or offenders depending on the source.
limitations: Different units must not be summed or divided without a valid common denominator.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse survey break
verified_claims: CSEW domestic-abuse estimates from year ending March 2024 use new questions and are not comparable with earlier question sets.
limitations: Long-term trends must not cross the questionnaire break.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse prevalence
verified_claims: An estimated 7.8% of people aged 16 years and over, around 3.8 million people, experienced domestic abuse in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: A national survey estimate is not an exact count of local incidents or parcels.

sources.name: Female and male prevalence estimates
verified_claims: The estimated last-year prevalence was 9.1% for females and 6.5% for males.
limitations: Survey sex-group estimates do not establish individual-level risk.

sources.name: Partner and family abuse distinction
verified_claims: Last-year prevalence was higher for partner or ex-partner abuse than for family abuse.
limitations: Relationship categories may overlap within an individual's lifetime experience.

sources.name: No significant annual change
verified_claims: There was no statistically significant annual change in overall domestic abuse, partner abuse or family abuse prevalence.
limitations: Numerical differences must not be labelled trends without statistical significance.

sources.name: Incident and crime distinction
verified_claims: Police domestic-abuse incidents include reports where investigation concludes that no notifiable crime occurred; recorded crimes are a subset.
limitations: Incident and crime totals must not be treated as duplicate-independent categories.

sources.name: Police-recorded domestic-abuse crimes
verified_claims: Police recorded 816,493 domestic-abuse-related crimes in the year ending March 2025, fewer than the previous year.
limitations: The decrease is likely influenced by changes in police recording practices and is not a direct prevalence measure.

sources.name: Share of police-recorded offences
verified_claims: Domestic-abuse-related crimes represented 15.4% of offences recorded by police in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: The share uses police-recorded offences and not all crime or all abuse experienced.

sources.name: Female victim representation
verified_claims: Females accounted for 72.1% of identified victims in police-recorded domestic-abuse-related crimes.
limitations: Police-recorded victim profiles can differ from population survey profiles because of reporting and recording.

sources.name: CPS referrals
verified_claims: Police referred 76,393 domestic-abuse-related suspects to the Crown Prosecution Service for charging decisions in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Referral counts are suspects, not crimes or unique victims.

sources.name: Police and CPS comparison boundary
verified_claims: Direct comparisons between police-recorded crime totals and CPS data cannot be made.
limitations: Sources cover different cohorts, units and processing periods.

sources.name: Non-referral outcome range
verified_claims: Police investigations may end with no further action, transfer, out-of-court resolution, cancellation or no identified suspect.
limitations: An absence from CPS referral data does not identify which alternative outcome occurred.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse suspects charged
verified_claims: The CPS charged 53,919 suspects in domestic-abuse-related cases in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: A charge is not a conviction and may relate to multiple allegations or defendants.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse charging rate
verified_claims: The CPS domestic-abuse charging rate was 79.9%, based on legal decisions within its defined denominator.
limitations: The charging rate is not charges divided by all police-recorded domestic-abuse crimes.

sources.name: Reasons not to charge
verified_claims: Non-charge decisions can reflect evidential insufficiency, public-interest considerations or inability of a victim to support prosecution.
limitations: A non-charge decision does not establish that the reported abuse did not occur.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse prosecutions
verified_claims: The CPS recorded 54,987 domestic-abuse-related prosecutions in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: Prosecution counts can include cases initiated in earlier periods.

sources.name: Conviction and non-conviction outcomes
verified_claims: Of domestic-abuse-related prosecutions, 41,070 resulted in convictions and 13,917 in non-convictions.
limitations: Case outcomes must not be assigned to specific police incidents without linkage.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse source comparability
verified_claims: Domestic-abuse sources are not directly comparable because they use different units, cohorts and time-to-progression windows.
limitations: The full system picture requires source-specific interpretation rather than a single conversion ratio.
